clue.text: Result of evacuation from warship evacuated and jacketed

indicators.note: 'and jacketed' says the emptied warship is then given a jacket, so its letters go inside the coat

parts.note: something jacketed has been put in a coat

indicators.note: an evacuated word has had its contents emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A naval scene: crew evacuated from a warship, bundled into jackets, and the result of the evacuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties the warship to its outer letters, and 'jacketed' supplies a coat round them. 'Result of evacuation' is toilet humour about a cow's bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow emptying its bowels leaves a dropping in the field, so the dropping is the result of bovine evacuation.

clue.text: Dubious heirs to Switzerland's treasure

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

indicators.note: dubious letters are doubtful, not to be trusted as they stand, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Questionable heirs laying claim to a Swiss fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the shuffled heirs onto CH, which comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to treasure something is to hold it dear and value it highly; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Moan, if drink's drunk hot

indicators.note: the drink has drunk (taken in) the letter for hot, so that letter sits inside it

parts.note: wine is a drink
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A complaint that the drink has been served warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is read as 'swallowed', not as the state of the drinker: the wine takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to complain in a peevish, drawn-out voice, which is a kind of moaning.

clue.text: Operatic heroine's number to finish up

indicators.note: the reversed piece is added to the first

parts.note: an aria is a musical number, a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for finish is read from bottom to top

parts.note: finish means end

explanation.surface: An opera heroine's big number brings the show to its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns END into DNE in this down clue, added to ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne is the title heroine of Richard Strauss's opera Ariadne auf Naxos, and of other operas on the Cretan princess.

clue.text: Navigator's bit of kit to turn brown within 31 days

indicators.note: within says one word is placed inside another, here inside the month

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated OCT
to tan is to turn brown in the sun

explanation.surface: A sailor's instrument goes brown from the sun inside a month.
explanation.walkthrough: '31 days' is a month, here October, which takes TAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is an instrument for measuring angles, used at sea for celestial navigation before the sextant.

clue.text: Investigator of death trap concealing nothing

indicators.note: concealing means the word for trap hides the other piece inside it

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An inquest suggests a death trap that hid nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'death trap' reads as one phrase, but 'Investigator of death' is the definition and 'trap' is CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who holds inquests into sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: A parasite receiving paper hat, originally from charitable institution

indicators.note: receiving means the parasite takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect
MS, a manuscript, is a paper

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word hat

explanation.surface: A parasite gets a paper hat from a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts the paper and the first of hat (by 'originally') inside the parasite, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse was a home founded by charity for the poor or elderly to live in free.

clue.text: One old racist party piercing Labour's protective wrapping

indicators.note: piercing means the first pieces push into the word for labour

parts.note: toil is labour, hard work
I, the Roman numeral, is one
the NF, the National Front, was a far-right British party prominent in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A political picture: a racist faction breaking into the Labour Party's protective shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour's' looks like the British party, but it is just toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet wrapped round food to protect and preserve it.

clue.text: Badly wanting a maypole to hire

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together in a jumbled, wrong order
wanting means lacking, so the letter a is left out of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: Someone badly wants a maypole they can rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a' is not desire: MAYPOLE lacking an A leaves MYPOLE, which 'Badly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to hire them for work; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Turmeric mostly spilled between food store and toilet as result of overconsumption

indicators.note: between places the scrambled spice letters in the gap separating the shop and the toilet

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
the MENS is a men's toilet

indicators.note: spilled letters are scattered and land in a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the spice is used

explanation.surface: Spice spilt between the deli and the gents, after too much of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the spice's final C, 'spilled' scrambles the rest to RIUMTRE, and 'between' sets that in the shop and the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The DTs are the shaking and hallucinations of alcohol withdrawal, brought on by long heavy drinking.

clue.text: Ordinary soldier to serve as commander in Biblical land

parts.note: a GI is an ordinary American soldier
to lead is to command

explanation.surface: A private soldier promoted to command in the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilead is a mountainous region east of the Jordan named in the Old Testament, famed for its balm.

clue.text: Food parcel causing bulge in the nether regions?

definitions.meaning: a packed container of food for a midday meal
British slang for the visible outline of a man's genitals in tight trousers

explanation.surface: A packed meal tucked somewhere it makes a suspicious lump.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cheeky British slang, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a box carrying a packed meal, and slang for a crotch bulge.

clue.text: Scotch queen protected from displaying facial hair

indicators.note: protected means the queen is shielded inside the drink

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A bearded monarch kept away from the Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskery is the adjective for having whiskers, so something bristly with facial hair.

clue.text: Took part, keeping pig in cupboard

indicators.note: keeping means the word for took part holds the pig inside it

parts.note: to side with someone is to take their part
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Someone joined in by hiding a pig in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took part' means took a side, giving SIDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a dining-room cabinet with cupboards and drawers below a flat top.

clue.text: Rake keeping back pound coin

indicators.note: keeping means the rake holds the next piece inside itself

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a debauched man

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for pound is read in reverse

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A libertine holding back a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the pound abbreviation to BL before the rake takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia, and coins are minted in it.

clue.text: Shostakovich and Elgar sheltering one of their ilk

indicators.note: sheltering means the composers' names hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Two composers taking a third under their wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel was a composer, like Shostakovich and Elgar, so he is one of their kind.

clue.text: About to embrace girls, touching bottom

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for about wraps round the next piece

parts.note: around means about
G is short for girls, as in a Girl Guide abbreviation

explanation.surface: A man about to hug some girls touches a bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching bottom' sounds like groping, but means a ship stuck on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat run aground is resting on the sea or river bed, so its keel touches the bottom.

clue.text: Revolutionary carrying round eagle's head, like a big cat

indicators.note: carrying means the revolutionary holds the round shape inside him

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian Revolution
O is round in shape

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of eagle

explanation.surface: A revolutionary carrying an eagle, as lion-like as a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts O inside LENIN; 'head' adds E from eagle at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and the lion is the classic big cat.

clue.text: Obstacle in path of form of speculation

indicators.note: in means the obstacle sits inside the path

parts.note: a route is a path
let means hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Something blocking the way on a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as an obstacle is an old sense, kept in the phrase 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance, a gamble, which is speculation in a loose sense.

clue.text: Pick up birds raised to follow soldiers

indicators.note: to follow means the reversed birds come after the soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the birds are read upwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Birds lifted into the air behind marching troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EMUS into SUME in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up where you left off is to carry on again, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Hun running amok craving divorce?

indicators.note: running amok is wild and disordered, so the letters scatter

parts.note: an itch is a craving

explanation.surface: A Hun on the rampage, longing for a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: divorce in the sense of uncoupling.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple a trailer or horse is, figuratively, to separate or part it from what it was joined to.

clue.text: Cream, mostly, and fan thereof, turning touchy

indicators.note: turning means the combined pieces are read from end to start
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for cream

parts.note: the elite is the cream, the best
a cat is a lover of cream

explanation.surface: Cream and the one who loves it turn touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ELITE to ELIT; 'turning' reverses ELITCAT. 'touchy' means of touch, not tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to touch, which a punning 'touchy' expresses.

clue.text: Four jabs administered through the looking-glass? Great!

indicators.note: jabs administered are given out, so their letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient given four injections on the other side of the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Jabberwocky in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, hence the reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll coined the exclamation 'O frabjous day!', meaning joyous or wonderful.

clue.text: Satirist's turned vehicle into gardening tool

indicators.note: into means the turned vehicle is set inside the tool

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool for weeding

indicators.note: turned means the vehicle's letters run backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A satirist turned his car into a gardening tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives RAC from CAR, which goes into HOE; 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a Roman poet whose Satires made him a model for later satirists.

clue.text: Nearly, nearly suffering disorder of internal organ

indicators.note: a word suffering disorder has its letters thrown out of order
the first Nearly means the second word is used without its last letter

explanation.surface: Something almost, almost going wrong with a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Nearly' trims the second to NEARL, which 'suffering disorder' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are internal organs.

clue.text: Nudity evens out autism twice after necessary adjustments?

indicators.note: adjustments to the pooled letters reorder them
evens out means the even-numbered letters of nudity are dropped, keeping the odd ones
twice means the word autism is written two times

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about nudity and autism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evens out' keeps NDT, the odd letters of nudity; with AUTISM twice they are rearranged, the definition doubling as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutatis mutandis is Latin for 'things being changed that have to be changed'.

clue.text: Proceed unsteadily with introduction to dark stranger

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of dark

parts.note: odder means stranger, more peculiar

explanation.surface: A tottering walk to meet a dark stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' is not a person but the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or move shakily, as frail elderly people may.

clue.text: Slope put on ice

definitions.meaning: to slope gently downward, as land or a seabed does
to set a plan aside, postponing it indefinitely

explanation.surface: A slippery slope put on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: to incline gradually, and to defer a project.
